title: Add UNIQUE(card_id, device_id, ts) on timecard_events + ignore-duplicates on insert
description:
Invariant 7 from incident-recovery design. Idempotent insertion is required for safe retry — without it, any partial-success (Supabase wrote the row but HTTP response was lost mid-flight) becomes a duplicate row on the next retry.

Schema migration:
  -- 023_timecard_events_uniq.sql (or next free number)
  alter table timecard_events
    add constraint timecard_events_uniq_tap
    unique (card_id, device_id, ts);

Backfill check first — any existing dupes will block the constraint:
  select card_id, device_id, ts, count(*)
  from timecard_events
  group by 1,2,3
  having count(*) > 1;
If dupes found, decide: keep oldest by ingestion order, or merge raw_payload arrays.

Bridge insert call gets the PostgREST upsert-ish header:
  headers["Prefer"] = "return=minimal,resolution=ignore-duplicates"
With this, retries that hit an already-inserted row return 2xx (no-op) instead of 409, so the bridge outbox cleanly deletes the queued row.

Also pair with hc4.1: the outbox DELETE-on-2xx logic relies on this — without it, a partial-success retry returns 409, the bridge's `raise_for_status()` flags it, and the row sits in the outbox forever even though it's already in Supabase.
notes:
2026-05-13: DB half applied.
- Found 1 dupe pair (manual ignored=true taps from 2026-04-27, admin double-click). Deleted later row id=58780b55-aa6c-4f20-bb09-a28c769e00ce.
- Applied migration 023_timecard_events_uniq_tap.sql -> `UNIQUE(card_id, device_id, ts)`. Confirmed via pg_constraint.
- File mirrored to repo at migration/023_timecard_events_uniq_tap.sql.

Client-side (bridge `Prefer: resolution=ignore-duplicates`) ships with hc4.1 PR — keep this issue open until that lands.
close_reason: Closed

title: Mosquitto persistence audit: survive broker host power loss
description:
Invariant 2 from incident-recovery design discussion. If broker host loses power, in-memory MQTT queue dies. Mosquitto default `autosave_interval=1800s` -> up to 30 minutes of queued QoS1 messages lost on power cut.

Action items:
- Locate Mosquitto config in the Portainer stack (likely `mosquitto.conf` in a volume mount)
- Confirm these settings:
    persistence true
    persistence_location /mosquitto/data/
    autosave_interval 30          # or `autosave_on_changes true`
    queue_qos0_messages false     # we don't use QoS0 for taps
    max_queued_messages 10000     # bigger than realistic outage backlog
- Confirm `/mosquitto/data/` is a named docker volume in docker-compose, not container ephemeral
- Test: stop bridge, publish N taps, hard-restart broker container, restart bridge, verify all N delivered

Pairs with hc4.3 (bridge clean_session=False) — both needed for broker-side durability.
notes:
2026-05-14: SHIPPED + verified by gold-plated test.

Configuration applied (Mosquitto 2.0.11 on 10.0.0.180):

  /etc/mosquitto/conf.d/01-persistence-tuning.conf:
    autosave_on_changes true
    max_queued_messages 10000
    max_inflight_messages 100

  /etc/mosquitto/mosquitto.conf (line 20, inside listener 1883 block
  because per_listener_settings true):
    queue_qos0_messages true

The queue_qos0_messages line was the missing piece. Reader publishes
QoS 0 (PubSubClient default), so without this, broker dropped
messages for absent subscribers even with persistent session.

Also moved /etc/mosquitto/conf.d/mosquitto.old (duplicate of main
config that was being parsed silently) to /etc/mosquitto/mosquitto.old.bak

Gold test result 2026-05-14 09:07:
- bridge stopped
- card 462EC200 tapped @ 08:07:09 UTC
- mosquitto restart while bridge still down
- bridge restarted -> session_present=True -> delivered tap with
  original ts preserved (id=20, attempts=0)

Acceptance: tap-during-broker-restart-during-bridge-down round-trip,
original ts preserved end-to-end. Pass.
close_reason: Persistence + queue_qos0_messages shipped; gold test passed with original ts preserved

title: Bridge: add durable outbox (SQLite) + retry on Supabase failure
description:
Root cause of 2026-05-13 incident. timecard-bridge has no buffer: failed POST to Supabase -> caught by `except Exception` -> `print(\"ERR\", ...)` -> message dropped forever.

Smoking gun from bridge logs (2026-05-13 ~05:00 UTC):
  ERR ... NameResolutionError ... Failed to resolve 'hguvsjpmiyeypfcuvvko.supabase.co'
  topic= carrwood/timecard payload_sample= {\"event\":\"tap\",\"card_id\":\"A66A9500\", ...}

DNS/WAN flap -> 3 known taps lost (A66A9500, A650B200, 1616BD00) even though readers, broker, and bridge container were all healthy.

Fix: in `bridge_mqtt_to_supabase.py`, replace one-shot `requests.post(...)` with a durable outbox:
- on_message: write payload + table + topic + first_seen_ts into local SQLite (e.g. /data/outbox.db, volume-mounted)
- background worker: drain oldest rows, POST to Supabase, delete on 2xx, retry-forever w/ exponential backoff on 5xx/network/DNS errors
- only ACK MQTT message (auto-ack on return from on_message is fine) AFTER outbox write commits — so a bridge crash before disk-write leaves QoS1 redelivery as the safety net

Repo: https://github.com/ukstevem/timecard-bridge (not on local disk yet)

Acceptance: kill WAN/DNS for 10 min during a test, tap 3 cards, restore WAN, verify all 3 land in `timecard_events` with original `ts`. Outbox.db survives container restart.
notes:
Local checkout: `C:\Dev\Timecard Database Reader\timecard-bridge\bridge_mqtt_to_supabase.py`

Re-read confirms: client_id=`timecard-bridge`, VERSION2 callback API, no clean_session set, on_message does parse -> supabase_insert -> on raise: `print("ERR" ...)` and drop.

Scope-expand: while in the file, also fix two adjacent silent-drop bugs found during incident review:
1. `except Exception as e` (line 87) catches Supabase HTTP 4xx the same as network/DNS. Outbox should split retryable (network/5xx, keep + backoff) vs permanent (4xx, move to dead-letter table + log loudly).
2. `iso_or_now_z` (lines 30-37) silently rewrites bad/missing ts to wall-clock. A malformed reader ts becomes "now" with no signal. Either reject + dead-letter, or stamp `raw_payload.ts_was_invalid=true` for forensics. Pairs with hc4.5.

Outbox table sketch (in /data/outbox.db SQLite, volume mounted):
  CREATE TABLE outbox (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    enqueued_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    last_attempt_at TEXT,
    attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    next_attempt_at TEXT,
    row_json TEXT NOT NULL
  );
  CREATE INDEX idx_outbox_next ON outbox(next_attempt_at) WHERE next_attempt_at IS NOT NULL;

  CREATE TABLE outbox_dead (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    failed_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    http_status INTEGER,
    error TEXT,
    row_json TEXT NOT NULL
  );

Worker drains FIFO with exponential backoff (e.g. 1s, 2s, 4s ... cap 60s) on retryable; moves to outbox_dead on permanent 4xx (other than 408/429).
Invariants from recovery-sequence design discussion (T0 net-down -> T1 power-cut -> T2 power-up no DB -> T3 DB back):

Invariant 1 — SQLite durability across power loss:
  PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
  PRAGMA synchronous=FULL;     -- fsync per commit, not NORMAL
  -- one COMMIT per outbox INSERT

Invariant 3 — outbox.db on named docker volume, not container ephemeral. Add to docker-compose.yaml:
  volumes:
    - timecard_outbox:/data
  ...
  volumes:
    timecard_outbox:

Invariant 4 — bridge clean_session=False + stable client_id (hc4.3). On power-up, broker replays its surviving queue into the bridge, which lands them in the outbox.

Invariant 5 — outbox dedupe key. Same tap can hit on_message twice (broker replay + the row we already had in outbox before crash). Add to outbox schema:
  UNIQUE(topic, recv_ts_ns, payload_sha256)
Or simpler: use Supabase UNIQUE (Invariant 7, hc4.9) as the authoritative dedupe and let outbox over-store. Belt + braces = both.

Invariant 6 — store raw MQTT bytes + topic + recv_ts in outbox, NOT the parsed `row` dict. Parse at drain time. If we ever fix a parser bug (e.g. hc4.5 NTP guard), the backlog auto-benefits. Current `parse()` normalises `event` and `actor` -> would lock in normalisation errors that we'd want to revisit on replay.

Revised outbox schema:
  CREATE TABLE outbox (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    recv_ts TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    topic TEXT NOT NULL,
    raw_bytes BLOB NOT NULL,
    payload_sha256 BLOB NOT NULL,
    attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    next_attempt_at TEXT,
    last_error TEXT,
    UNIQUE(topic, recv_ts, payload_sha256)
  );
  CREATE INDEX idx_outbox_ready ON outbox(next_attempt_at, id);

Worker pseudocode:
  while True:
    row = SELECT * FROM outbox
          WHERE (next_attempt_at IS NULL OR next_attempt_at <= datetime('now'))
          ORDER BY id LIMIT 1
    if not row: sleep(1); continue
    parsed = parse(row.topic, row.raw_bytes.decode())  # at drain time
    try:
        supabase_insert(parsed)   # with Prefer: resolution=ignore-duplicates
        DELETE FROM outbox WHERE id = row.id
    except retryable:             # network, DNS, 5xx, 408, 429
        UPDATE outbox SET attempts++, next_attempt_at=now+backoff(attempts), last_error=str(e)
    except permanent:             # 4xx other than 408/429
        INSERT INTO outbox_dead SELECT * FROM outbox WHERE id=row.id
        DELETE FROM outbox WHERE id=row.id
        log.warn(...)

Reader power-loss caveat: if reader itself loses power, taps during the dark window are never published — outbox can't help. UPS on reader hardware is the only mitigation, out of scope here. hc4.4 (reader NVS buffer) only addresses reader-alive-but-no-network.
close_reason: Closed

title: Epic: Timecard ingestion resilience
description:
Network outage 2026-05-13 AM (testing phase): staff tapped cards but no rows landed in Supabase timecard_events; whos-in panel shows everyone OUT. Goal: make tap pipeline survive WiFi / broker / Supabase outages without losing taps.

Pipeline as observed:
  reader (M5 Core2 + WS1850S, Timecard.ino) -> MQTT broker (10.0.0.180:1883, Mosquitto in Portainer) -> ??? bridge -> Supabase timecard_events -> view employees_whos_in_now

Three independent failure segments, each needs its own resilience:
  1. reader -> broker         (reader-side offline buffer + replay)
  2. broker -> bridge          (QoS >=1, persistent session, stable client_id)
  3. bridge -> Supabase        (durable outbox: SQLite/disk queue + retry)

Child issues track each segment plus the audit work needed first.

Recovery path for past incidents already exists: record_manual_taps RPC (migration 017) via /hours admin page.
notes:
2026-05-13 investigation complete. Root cause = bridge has no durable outbox.

Pipeline as deployed:
- Reader (M5 Core2 + WS1850S, fw v0.6.0, device_id=carr-tc-02) -> publishes to broker on topic `carrwood/timecard` QoS 1
- Broker: Mosquitto on 10.0.0.180:1883, Portainer stack alongside `timecard-bridge` and `mqtt-status-bridge` containers
- Bridge: https://github.com/ukstevem/timecard-bridge subscribes carrwood/{jobcard,timecard}, foxwood/timecard QoS 1 -> POST to Supabase `timecard_events`
- Recovery: `record_manual_taps` RPC (migration 017) via `/hours` admin page

Confirmed in bridge logs: at outage time DNS failed for Supabase host. Bridge caught the exception and dropped 3 taps (A66A9500, A650B200, 1616BD00). MQTT delivery itself was fine — QoS 1 + bridge online = broker handed them over cleanly.

Children:
- hc4.1 P1 bug: bridge SQLite outbox (the real fix for today's failure mode)
- hc4.2 P1 task: locate v0.6.0 firmware src (Timecard.ino in local repo is stale prototype)
- hc4.3 P2 bug: bridge clean_session=False + stable client_id (covers bridge-restart-during-outage)
- hc4.4 P2 feature: reader SPIFFS buffer + non-blocking reconnect + QoS 1 (covers LAN/broker outage)
- hc4.5 P3 bug: reader NTP-not-synced guard (saw a 1999 timestamp on 2026-05-12)
- hc4.6 P2 task: manual recovery of the 3 lost taps from today
- hc4.7 P2 chore: cred hygiene (WiFi pwd in firmware, RDS pwd in databaseconnection.py)
close_reason: All 10 children closed. Timecard ingestion fully resilient end-to-end: reader SD pending queue, broker QoS0 persistence + queue, bridge SQLite outbox with retry/dead-letter, DB UNIQUE constraint with ignore-duplicates. Gold-plated test passed 2026-05-14.

title: Reader: SPIFFS/NVS offline buffer + non-blocking reconnect + QoS 1
description:
Segment 1 resilience: today's outage was WAN-only so readers + broker were unaffected, but a LAN/broker drop currently loses taps silently AND makes the reader unresponsive.

Current behaviour (firmware v0.6.0, inferred — confirm against actual source once located, see sibling task):
- Publishes QoS 0, not retained (per stale prototype Timecard.ino:78) -> broker won't ack, no redelivery
- `connectWiFi()` / `connectMQTT()` are blocking `while` loops -> during outage the RFID poll doesn't run -> card taps in that window aren't sampled at all (worse than dropped — never seen)

Design:
- Replace blocking reconnect with state-machine: scan loop runs always, MQTT publish enqueues to local store on failure
- Local store: NVS or SPIFFS ring buffer of N tap records {card_id, ts (device NTP UTC), firmware}
- Publish QoS 1 so broker holds them across short subscriber gaps too
- On reconnect: drain oldest -> newest, original `ts` preserved

Requires the v0.6.0 source repo (sibling task).
notes:
2026-05-13 (after hc4.2 findings): file/line refs in production firmware.

Path: C:\Dev\Timecard Database Reader\Timeclock_0_5\Timeclock_0_5.ino

Current state:
- SD-card logging EXISTS at lines 383-395 (`appendLineToSD`). Writes JSON payload to /timecard/YYYY-MM-DD.csv with 90-day retention. So every tap is already durably captured on the device.
- Publish flow at lines 534-574: tries `mqtt.publish()`, on fail does one reconnect attempt + retry (lines 554-564), then gives up. SD-write success is what the UI banner reports as "success" — but the SD entry is never republished.
- Loop reconnect logic at lines 644-651: reconnects MQTT every 5s when WiFi up but MQTT down, but only for new taps — no pending-queue drain.

So the gap isn't "no buffer" — it's "buffer exists (SD) but never drained back to MQTT after reconnect". Cleaner-scoped fix:

1. Separate file /timecard/pending.jsonl (append-only, line-per-tap) updated in publishAndLog when mqtt.publish() fails (after the existing one-shot retry).
2. On successful publish, mark the corresponding line as sent (rewrite file? Or use a simple "drained-up-to byte offset" pointer file).
3. On every loop iteration where mqtt.connected() flipped false->true, run `drainPending()` — read lines from offset, publish each, advance offset.
4. Bound pending.jsonl size with rotation if it grows past N MB.

CSV remains for human readability + the bridge outbox is now the primary durability layer, so this is a defense-in-depth for the rare case where reader is up but broker is unreachable for long enough that QoS1 broker queue overflows or session drops.

ALSO: blocking-reconnect concern in the stale Timecard.ino prototype is NOT present in 0.6.0 — connectWiFi/connectMQTT have timeouts (lines 485-528) and the main loop never blocks on them. Update the issue title to reflect actual gap: "Reader: drain SD-buffered taps on MQTT reconnect".

Blocked by hc4.10 (firmware needs git first so the PR has somewhere to go).
2026-05-14: SHIPPED in firmware v0.7.0/0.7.1/0.7.2 + verified end-to-end.

Repo: https://github.com/ukstevem/timecard-reader-firmware

Implemented:
- /timecard/pending.jsonl outbox file (line-per-tap JSON payload)
- appendPending() called from publishAndLog() when mqtt.publish() fails
- drainPending() runs on MQTT-up edge OR every 30s while pending non-empty
- pendingHasContent() cheap check used as guard before drain
- UI banner now distinguishes Sent / Saved offline / FAILED with local HH:MM
- Speaker volume bumped (SPEAKER_VOLUME=220) for clearer cue

Important interaction with hc4.8: with mosquitto queue_qos0_messages
true, broker queues QoS 0 messages for offline persistent-session
subscribers, so the most common failure mode (bridge restart while
reader online) is now handled broker-side without needing the reader
SD queue to engage. The reader SD queue covers WiFi/broker-unreachable
cases where mqtt.publish() actually returns false.

QoS 1 upgrade for the reader publish path was NOT done -
PubSubClient lacks clean outbound QoS 1 support and library swap is
larger scope. With queue_qos0_messages + SD pending queue, end-to-end
guarantees are equivalent.

Gold test (hc4.8 notes) proves the tap-during-bridge-down case lands
in Supabase with original ts.

title: Bridge: set clean_session=False + keep stable client_id
description:
Secondary resilience gap. `bridge_mqtt_to_supabase.py` does not set `clean_session` -> paho default = True. If the bridge container restarts (deploy, crash, OOM, healthcheck kill), the broker drops the queued QoS-1 messages for client_id `timecard-bridge` instead of holding them for redelivery.

Today's incident did not exercise this path (bridge stayed connected throughout, MQTT delivered fine). But pair this with the outbox change and a bridge restart during WAN outage stays safe: broker holds while bridge is down, bridge drains outbox on reconnect.

Fix: `mqtt.Client(..., clean_session=False)` on the v3.1.1 API, or equivalent in v5. Verify Mosquitto has `persistence true` and the volume survives container restart.

Acceptance: stop bridge, publish 3 msgs to `carrwood/timecard`, start bridge, verify all 3 delivered.
close_reason: Closed

title: Refactor employees_daily_hours to use per-employee shift_pattern
description: Currently the function takes p_shift_start/p_shift_end as parameters with global defaults. With employee_shift_pattern + employee_shift_pattern_day tables in place, the function should LEFT JOIN through to the assigned pattern's per-weekday row to get day_start/day_finish/lunch_start/lunch_finish for each (employee, work_date). Rules: (1) employees with NULL shift_pattern_id continue to use the global default constants; (2) is_working_day for an employee = their pattern has a row for that weekday (or fall back to Mon-Fri default); (3) worked_minutes should subtract unpaid lunch minutes (paid_lunch=false) overlapping the worked time; (4) late_minutes/early_finish_minutes computed against that day's specific day_start/day_finish; (5) function function-arg defaults remain for callers that want a fixed shift override.

title: Reader: refuse to publish if NTP not synced (1999 timestamp guard)
description:
Bridge log on 2026-05-12 captured this tap:
  OK carrwood timecard 963F9500 1999-11-30T00:00:17Z

Reader's NTP hadn't synced when card was tapped — published a 1999 timestamp. Downstream ingestion accepted it. Anything that buckets by date/week (whos-in, /hours, Bradford) will silently mis-bucket these.

Fix in reader firmware: in `publishScan()`, if `time(nullptr) < 1704067200` (2024-01-01 UTC), refuse to publish — either drop with visible UI/buzzer warning or enqueue to offline buffer (sibling task) and republish after NTP comes back with a corrected ts (hard — clock was wrong, so the buffered ts is wrong; simplest is "drop + warn user to retap once display clears").

Belt-and-braces also: bridge could reject any payload with ts < 2024-01-01 -> log to a `timecard_events_ignored` style table (migration 018 already exists for this pattern). Cheap second line of defence.
close_reason: NTP guard at start of publishAndLog (v0.7.3)
